turns.human_input: I'm the IT manager at a 60-person company and I just got an alert — our customer database might have been exfiltrated. Login anomalies at 2am, unusual outbound traffic to an IP in Eastern Europe. This could have 8,000 customer records. I don't have a breach response plan. What do I do?!
turns.ai_response: Isolate first, investigate second. Immediately segment or take offline the affected systems — pull the network cable or block the external IP at the firewall right now to stop active exfiltration if it's still happening. Do not reboot or wipe anything; you need forensic state preserved. Loop in your CEO in the next 15 minutes — this is no longer just an IT incident, it's a legal and compliance event. You almost certainly have breach notification obligations: most US states require notifying affected customers within 30-72 hours depending on the state, and if you handle any EU data, GDPR is 72 hours to the supervisory authority. You need outside legal counsel who handles data breach response, today. Do you know what data was in that database — any payment card data, SSNs, health info?
